observations.text:
IntroductionLiteracy is a determinant of mental health, wellbeing, and social participation. Although literacy interventions improve educational and socioeconomic outcomes, their effects on mental health and social participation are poorly evidenced. We aimed to assess the feasibility and acceptability of a group-based literacy and numeracy intervention and explore its effects on literacy, mental health, numeracy, wellbeing, and social participation. We also estimated implementation costs.

MethodsWe conducted a mixed-methods study using an uncontrolled pre-post design among women in low- income urban communities in Lucknow, India. A total of 115 women were recruited to a 17-week group literacy intervention using the Accelerating Learning for All literacy intervention. Outcomes measured at baseline, midline, and endline used literacy and numeracy assessments and validated scales of mental distress, wellbeing, and social participation. Quantitative data were analysed using multilevel mixed-effects models. Qualitative interviews and focus groups were analysed thematically. Costs were calculated per participant.

ResultsThe intervention was feasible and acceptable with functional recruitment of 71% (82/115), 74/82 participants (90%) completed it (retention), and mean attendance of 69% of scheduled sessions. In multilevel mixed-effects models, mean literacy scores increased by 29.5 (95% CI: 23.6, 35.3) between baseline and endline, while mean mental distress (SRQ20) decreased by 3.4 (95% CI: 2.2, 4.6), mean mental wellbeing (WEMWBS) improved by 2.6 (95% CI: 0.1, 5.1), while social exclusion (P scale) declined by 4.1 (95% CI: 1.6, 6.5). Qualitatively, participants described greater confidence, autonomy, financial literacy, and social support. Implementation enablers included local facilitators.

Implementation cost was US$25 per participant.

ConclusionThis low-cost literacy intervention was feasible and acceptable for women in low-income urban communities in India. Findings provide preliminary evidence of improvements in literacy, mental health, and social participation. Controlled studies are needed to establish causal effects, long-term outcomes, and scalability.

What is already known on this topicLiteracy is a recognised upstream determinant of mental health through its influence on education, social participation, and health literacy. There is almost no evidence examining whether literacy interventions for women can directly improve mental health and wellbeing, particularly among highly disadvantaged populations. Further, little is known about the feasibility and effectiveness of brief literacy interventions in low-income, disadvantaged urban settings, where women with limited or no literacy skills are disproportionately concentrated.

What this study addsThis study shows that a brief literacy intervention among low-income women in informal urban North India is both feasible and acceptable when implemented by local community members. It shows this can be implemented with modest financial cost (around US$25 per person). It shows that participation in the intervention was associated with improved social participation, mental health and mental wellbeing.

How the study might affect research, practice or policyHaving demonstrated feasibility and acceptability, together with the promising associations observed in this study, it provides a strong rationale for rigorous randomised controlled trials to establish causality and determine whether this low-cost intervention can deliver meaningful and sustainable improvements in mental health and wellbeing at scale.

metadata.summary: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to profile the transcriptional landscape of ventricular tissue in a Sprague-Dawley rat model of myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). Two groups were analyzed: an I/R control group and a group treated with the pro-lymphangiogenic polymeric formulation PD-DN. Ventricular tissues were collected from both groups at three time points post-injury — 3, 5, and 7 days — to capture the temporal dynamics of cardiac repair. Single-cell suspensions were processed using the 10x Genomics Chromium platform with Illumina NovaSeq sequencing. Our analysis revealed temporally orchestrated changes in endothelial, immune, and fibroblast cell populations. The data provide insights into how PD-DN-driven lymphangiogenesis reprograms the cardiac microenvironment to facilitate functional recovery.

metadata.summary: Background. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Our goal was to determine the effects of the dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 inhibitor sotagliflozin (SOTA) on myocardial remodeling, diastolic function, mitochondrial gene expression and oxidative stress in mice with HCM due to the tropomyosin E180G mutation (E180G). Methods. Male E180G and non-carrier (NC) mice 7-8 weeks old were randomized to SOTA formulated in the chow (30 mg/kg chow) or control diet (CD) for 8 weeks. Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography at baseline, and after 4 and 8 weeks of treatment. At 8 weeks mice were sacrificed to assess myocardial histology, RNA expression, oxidative stress and oxidative sulfonylation of sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase (SERCA). Results. At baseline E180G mice had myocardial hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction and atrial enlargement - all of which worsened over the next 8 weeks. In E180G mice treatment with SOTA for 8 weeks prevented further LV hypertrophy and atrial enlargement, decreased interstitial fibrosis and normalized diastolic function. Mitochondrial gene sets were downregulated, and oxidative stress was increased and associated with oxidative sulfonylation of SERCA at C674. SOTA treatment upregulated mitochondrial gene sets and prevented the increases in oxidative stress and SERCA oxidation. Upregulated fibrosis gene sets in E180G hearts were not affected by SOTA. Conclusion. In E180G HCM mice downregulation of mitochondrial gene sets is associated with increased oxidative stress and oxidative modification of SERCA. In E180G hearts, SOTA corrected the HCM phenotype, normalized diastolic function, upregulated mitochondrial gene sets, and decreased oxidative stress and SERCA oxidation. Upregulation of mitochondrial gene sets leading to improved mitochondrial function may improve energetics and decrease oxidative stress. Oxidative stress leads to oxidative modification of SERCA and stimulation of fibrosis pathways which may play a significant role in HCM, and thus provide an opportunity for therapeutic intervention with agents that improve mitochondrial function and/or decrease oxidative stress.

observations.title: Dual SGLT1 and 2 inhibition with sotagliflozin decreases oxidative stress in mice with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy due to tropomyosin E180G mutation

observations.text: The multistage model of carcinogenesis explains the steep rise of cancer incidence with age through accumulated events, and reliability theory extends this principle to systems whose failure requires several components. We asked whether the same idea could explain why chronic diseases differ in how rapidly incidence rises with age, and whether multimorbidity could independently reveal the processes involved. In UK Biobank, linked health records allowed pre-assessment disease co-occurrence and subsequent incidence to be analysed separately. Using generative representation learning, we derived 16 functional units (FUs) from co-occurrence patterns across 232 diagnoses in 502,355 participants. For each diagnosis, we counted linked FUs and compared this breadth with subsequent incidence. Diagnoses linked to more FUs showed steeper age dependence of incidence (Spearman{rho} = 0.50; 0.46 among 196 diagnoses with rising hazards), and this relationship persisted in an age-free representation. The FUs had distinct genetic architectures, with lead-variant directions preserved in FinnGen and the Million Veteran Program. Their GWAS reached 34 regions missed by diagnosis and BMI comparators, while fine-mapping and molecular evidence connected FU loci to candidate genes enriched for approved drug targets. Together, these results extend a multistage principle from cancer to chronic disease and show that multimorbidity structure explains variation in age-dependent incidence.
observations.title: Functional organization of multimorbidity links chronic disease incidence to shared genetic architecture

observations.text: Rationale Recent viral metagenomic studies have revealed a broad repertoire of enzyme encoding genes in Phycodnaviridae, whose contributions to viral replication and host infection remain poorly understood. These genes may expand the metabolic repertoire of viruses during infection of green algal hosts. Because neither the roles of these proteins during infection nor their subcellular localization have been experimentally characterized, comparative sequence, structural, and biochemical analyses done in silico can generate testable hypotheses on structure, function and localization. Methods In a recent viral metagenomic dataset, we identified viral homologues of two eukaryotic enzymes involved in bilin biosynthesis: heme oxygenase-1 (vHMOX1) and Phycocyanobilin:Ferredoxin oxidoreductase (vPcyA). Viral and algal homologues were compared through sequence analyses and AlphaFold3 structural predictions. Predicted biochemical properties were analyzed for their compatibility with subcellular compartments. Active site architecture and putative substrate binding were compared between viral and algal proteins using homologous structures deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB). Results Viral HMOX1 and PcyA sequences are truncated compared to algal homologues, lacking the N-terminal extension associated with chloroplastic targeting. However biochemical properties, including isoelectric point and surface charge distribution, are compatible with localization in chloroplast. Structural comparisons reveal modifications in the viral HMOX1 active sites, including altered substrate binding and substitutions of key residues, likely indicating modified heme-binding properties. In addition to these modifications, chloroplastic ferredoxin interaction predictions show compatibility for use of this electron donor. In contrast, vPcyA models show no significant differences with their algal counterparts. Conclusions Predicted active site remodeling in vHMOX1 suggests that these viral homologues may have evolved distinct heme-binding properties. Unlike vPcyA, vHMOX1 homologs appear to have diverged more substantially from their algal counterparts, potentially reflecting functional specialization in the viral infection context.
observations.title: Analysis of Phycodnaviridae Tetrapyrrole Enzymes: Subcellular Localization and Functional Divergence from Host Homologs

metadata.summary: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is a major cause of myocardial infarction and stroke. However, the precise drivers of plaque destabilisation remain elusive. We hypothesised that antigen-driven, autoimmune-like T cell responses are central to the destabilisation and rupture of atherosclerotic plaques. To dissect T cell responses specifically in unstable compared to stable plaques, we leveraged near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) imaging-guided dissection of human carotid plaques and our tandem stenosis model in mice. We applied single-cell multi-omics to study T cell differentiation states and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires. T cell responses in unstable versus stable atherosclerosis were distinct. Unstable human plaques contained highly expanded, autoimmune-like CD8+ T cells with markedly increased cytotoxic signatures, reduced exhaustion and distinct clonal repertoires compared to stable regions. Most plaque CD8+ T cells exhibited a pronounced tissue-resident transcriptional program. Autoimmune-like cytotoxic and tissue-resident CD8+ T cell responses were also evident in murine atherosclerosis, where restricting the activation of antigen-driven CD8+ T cells prevented plaque destabilisation.

observations.title: Autoimmune-like T Cell Responses Drive Atherosclerotic Plaque Instability

metadata.summary: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) exhibit limited efficacy against lung cancer brain metastases, often resulting in rapid and inevitable resistance. However, the unique mechanisms driving this brain microenvironment-specific therapeutic failure remain elusive. Here, utilizing in vivo orthotopic models and single-cell RNA sequencing, we reveal that targeted therapy induces a distinct, metabolically hyperactive senescent cell subpopulation that drives rapid EGFR-TKI tolerance in brain metastasis. We identify the molecular chaperone CRYAB as an indispensable driver specifically upregulated within this senescent persister state. Mechanistically, CRYAB physically interacts with VDAC2 at the outer mitochondrial membrane, promoting endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria tethering and calcium influx. This CRYAB-VDAC2 axis orchestrates adaptive mitochondrial fission, hyperactivating oxidative metabolism while simultaneously shielding（preventing？） senescent cells from fatal oxidative stress. Genetic or pharmacological blockade of mitochondrial fission completely abolishes CRYAB-mediated therapeutic resistance. Therapeutically, we demonstrate that a 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) dietary intervention acts as a potent in vivo senolytic strategy, directly dismantling the CRYAB-dependent resistance network, eradicating senescent persister cells, and synergistically prolonging overall survival when combined with Osi. Furthermore, high baseline CRYAB expression in pre-treatment primary lung biopsies clinically predicts lower intracranial objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival in a cohort of advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. Collectively, our study uncovers a novel CRYAB-VDAC2-mitochondrial fission axis that enforces therapy-induced senescence and highlights 25HC dietary intervention as a highly translatable combinatorial strategy to overcome EGFR-TKI resistance in brain metastasis.

observations.title: CRYAB-driven mitochondrial fission induces senescence to promote adaptive resistance to EGFR-TKI in LUAD brain metastasis

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

observations.title: Spatial genome and transcriptome co-mapping reveals clonal heterogeneity in tumor tissue [RNA-Seq]

observations.text: Predicting cellular response to perturbations is key to understanding biological mechanisms and selecting therapeutic targets. However, generalizing across cellular contexts, perturbations, and experimental datasets remains challenging due to incomplete representations of the system being perturbed and the difficulty of measuring true perturbation effects within that system. We introduce PIE, a model that addresses these limitations by reformulating the learning task around population level perturbation effects and incorporating auxiliary inputs that better characterize the biological system. PIE directly predicts differentially expressed genes and changes in gene expression for each (context, perturbation) pair, using external biological knowledge, baseline gene expression, and observed perturbation responses. Its architecture accommodates input sources with variable feature sets and predicts effects on genes seen and unseen during training. On the Replogle Nadig dataset, PIE achieves state of the art performance on most metrics across all tested generalization settings, including the most challenging setting where both the context and perturbation are unseen during training. For predicting differentially expressed genes, PIE achieves 1.2 to 3.2 times the AUPRC of the strongest baseline in each setting: across unseen contexts, perturbations, experimental datasets, and jointly unseen contexts and perturbations. Overall, PIE provides a framework for generalizing perturbation effects across diverse experimental conditions.
observations.title: PIE: Generalizing perturbation effects across unseen perturbations, contexts and datasets

observations.text:
IntroductionIn July 2025, WHO launched the "3 by 35" Initiative calling on countries to increase real prices of tobacco, alcohol, and sugary drinks by at least 50% by 2035 to secure an additional $ 1 trillion in public revenue. While the effectiveness of excise taxes and prices in reducing tobacco use is well-documented, the feasibility of this call to action has not been evaluated empirically across the world.

MethodsTrend changes in countries nominal and inflation-adjusted retail prices were investigated using the most-sold brand of cigarettes over windows ranging from 2 to 16 years over the period 2008-2024, derived from nine editions of the World Health Organization Report on the Global Tobacco Epidemic. Statistical models of the association of cigarette excise taxes and prices from the panel of 195 countries were estimated. The frequencies of cigarette prices rising by at least 20% and 50% over preceding periods was estimated, and the length of time countries would need to reach these targets based on past trends were predicted.

ResultsOver one-fifth of nominal cigarettes prices (and up to 40% in WHOs African region) were sticky across successive periods, even in countries with high overall consumer price inflation. Between 2008 and 2024, inflation-adjusted international dollar cigarette prices rose at a least squares annual trend growth rate of 2{middle dot}9% (95% UI 2{middle dot}8-3{middle dot}0%) Excise tax increases strongly predict price increases. One-third of countries saw real prices at least 50% higher than 10 years prior.

ConclusionMany of the instances of real price increases of 50% or more over 10-year periods occurred without countries implementing a conscious strategy to raise taxes. It is feasible to achieve and even surpass WHOs 3 by 35 call to action for tobacco if countries strategize and accelerate tobacco tax increases.

What is already knownPrevious research has evaluated the impact of cigarette and tobacco taxation and found that prices respond to higher excise taxes. However, whether price increases match, exceed or fall short of general price inflation in a country is an empirical question, with some evidence that taxes are over-shifted in high-income settings and that prices tend to be higher in countries with specific (per unit) taxes. In the policy setting, the Task Force on Fiscal Policy for Health modeled the impact of higher taxes that raise inflation-adjusted prices by at least 50% on reducing the consumption of tobacco. The World Health Organizations database of cigarette product prices and taxes collected every two years is comprehensive and permits analysis covering many more low- and middle-income countries and years than commercial databases.

What this study addsThe study examined the feasibility of WHOs global call to raise real tobacco prices using all data from available reports of the WHO Report on the Global Tobacco Epidemic from 2008-24. Analysis not previously conducted at this scale (16 years, more than 180 countries) include an examination of the stickiness of nominal cigarette prices, calculation of trends in nominal and real international prices, calculation of the extent of real price increases over multiple time windows, and estimation of country-specific trends real price changes.

How this study might affect research, practice or policyThis study finds that nominal cigarette prices were sticky over short time windows in many countries and that globally, real cigarette prices rose on average 2{middle dot}9% annually. It affirms that excise taxes on cigarettes tend to be over-shifted to prices (that is, a 1 dollar increase in tax increases prices by more than a dollar) especially when specific excise taxes were introduced or increased. One-third of countries saw real cigarette prices rise 50% or more over 10 years, but applying historical trend rates of real price growth based on their 2008-2024 experience indicated that many other countries would fall short of raising prices by 50%. Countries at all income levels have the potential for large cigarette price increases of 50% or more, but will have to accelerate their efforts substantially to achieve the WHO 3 by 35 global call.
observations.title: Nominal and real cigarette Price trends from a global dataset, 2008-2024 and implications for the World Health Organization's 3 by 35 initiative: a longitudinal study and forecasting analysis

metadata.summary: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is an inherited tumor predisposition syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in TSC1 or TSC2. We generated a heterozygous TSC2-mutant Yucatan minipig carrying the recurrent pathogenic TSC2 p.Arg505* variant and characterized its cardiac phenotype using histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and RNA sequencing. metadata.summary: The molecular and cellular processes leading to aortic aneurysm development in Marfan syndrome (MFS) remain poorly understood. We examined the changes of aortic cell populations and gene expression in MFS. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) on ascending aortic aneurysm tissues from patients with MFS (n=3) and age-matched non-aneurysmal control tissues from cardiac donors and recipients (n=4). The expression of key molecules was confirmed by immunostaining. Diverse populations of smooth muscle cells (SMCs), fibroblasts, and endothelial cell (EC) were detected in the aortic wall. Aortic tissues from MFS showed alterations of cell populations with increased de-differentiated proliferative SMCs compared to controls. Furthermore, there was a downregulation of MYOCD and MYH11 in SMCs, and an upregulation of COL1A1/2 in fibroblasts in MFS samples compared to controls. We also examined TGF-β signaling, an important pathway in aortic homeostasis. We found that TGFB1 was significantly upregulated in two fibroblast clusters in MFS tissues. However, TGF-β receptor genes (predominantly TGFBR2) and SMAD genes were downregulated in SMCs, fibroblasts, and ECs, indicating impairment in TGF-β signaling in MFS. Despite upregulation of TGFB1, the rest of the canonical TGF-β pathway was consistently downregulated in MFS, indicating a potential compromise of TGF-β signaling and lack of stimulus for SMC differentiation.

observations.title: Single-cell Analysis of Aneurysmal Aortic Tissue in Patients With Marfan Syndrome Reveals Dysfunctional TGF-β Signaling

metadata.summary: Fibroblast differentiation into matrix-producing, contractile myofibroblasts is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but whether these changes precede differentiation or arise from the activated phenotype remains unclear. To define when transcriptional remodeling emerges after TGFβ stimulation, we performed bulk RNA-seq on cardiac fibroblasts treated with TGFβ or bFGF for 1, 6, 12, 24, or 48 h. These findings support a phased, time-dependent remodeling of the cardiac fibroblast transcriptome in response to TGFβ relative to bFGF in which an initially limited response occurs at 1 h, expands substantially by 6 h, and subsequently encompasses cell cycle regulation, stress responses, developmental- and differentiation-associated programs, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix remodeling.

metadata.summary: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/− mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II–treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/− mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility–HFpEF interactions.

observations.title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency

observations.text:
ObjectiveTo evaluate whether the well-established age-related reduction in antral follicle counts (AFC) is greater among women with higher concentrations of endocrine-disrupting chemicals.

DesignProspective cohort study using the doubly robust (DR) learner, a flexible machine learning method that models the relationship between an exposure and outcome of interest and identifies potential modifiers of this relation.

SubjectsSeven hundred seventy-five women aged 18-45 years enrolled in The Environment and Reproductive Health (EARTH) Study at the Massachusetts General Hospital Fertility Center, Boston, USA, between 2004 and 2019.

ExposureAge at AFC assessment calculated as the date of antral follicle scan minus the patients birthdate, categorized into <35 years or [≥]35 years. We assessed urinary concentrations of 16 endocrine-disrupting chemicals, including 11 urinary phthalate metabolites, 3 urinary parabens, urinary bisphenol A, and hair mercury, as potential modifiers of the age-AFC association.

Main Outcome MeasuresAFC assessed by transvaginal ultrasonography.

ResultsIn this cohort of 775 women, 43% were less than 35 years of age. Women greater than or equal to aged 35 years had lower AFC (mean [SD]: 11.63 [6.24] vs. 16.89 [8.64]) Four endocrine-disrupting chemicals significantly modified the age-AFC association. Women with higher urinary mono-isobutyl phthalate (MiBP), monocarboxyisooctyl phthalate (MCOP), and mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP) concentrations experienced stronger negative associations between age and AFC. Analyses revealed that the age-AFC association strengthened, declining at a faster rate when MiBP, MCOP, or MEHP concentrations were higher. Women with higher hair Hg concentrations experienced weaker negative associations between age and AFC. The remaining 12 endocrine-disrupting chemicals did not modify the age-AFC relationship.

ConclusionSelect phthalate metabolites, specifically MiBP, MCOP, and MEHP, were associated with a modified age-related decline in ovarian reserve in a dose-dependent manner. These findings, though limited, add to the growing evidence that certain phthalates are associated with a steeper age-related decline in AFC.

What this study addsUsing the DR-Learner, a flexible machine learning approach designed to identify effect modifiers among a large set of candidates, we evaluated whether 16 endocrine-disrupting chemicals modify the well-established association between age and ovarian reserve. Three phthalate metabolites (MiBP, MCOP, MEHP) strengthened the negative age-antral follicle count association; for MiBP and MCOP this pattern was curvilinear and dose-dependent, with apparent concentration thresholds above which the age-related decline accelerated. Hair mercury was associated with a weaker negative association, possibly reflecting protective effects of seafood-derived omega-3 fatty acids. We discuss important limitations, but note that our findings add to evidence that higher phthalate concentrations accompany a stronger negative age-AFC association.
observations.title: Environmental Chemicals as Modifiers of the Association between Age and Ovarian Reserve

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

observations.title: Spatial genome and transcriptome co-mapping reveals clonal heterogeneity in tumor tissue [DNA-Seq]

metadata.summary: Heart failure (HF) is a growing global health crisis with a persistently poor prognosis, increasingly recognized as an inflammatory disease driven by CD4+ T lymphocytes that promote cardiac fibrosis and stiffness. Current therapies fail to address this immune component effectively. Here, we introduce first-in-class, drug-free Nano-Immuno-Metabolic Modulators (NIMMs) that ameliorate fibrosis by systemically reprogramming macrophage metabolism to curb pro-fibrotic T cell responses. Through high-throughput screening, we identified a lead candidate, NIMM22, which accumulates in the spleen and lymph nodes and potently upregulates macrophage arginase-1 expression. This metabolic shift depletes local L-arginine, suppressing CD4+ T cell effector function and their subsequent recruitment to the heart. NIMM22 treatment alleviated fibrosis and restored cardiac function across multiple murine cardiomyopathy models, including hypertensive and genetic disease. Chronic administration revealed no systemic toxicity or broad immune suppression, a safety profile confirmed in non-human primates. Our work establishes a new paradigm for cargo-free nanotherapeutics that modulate the cardiosplenic axis, offering a targeted, immunotherapy-like strategy with broad potential for treating cardiac and other immune-mediated fibrotic diseases.

observations.title: Cargoless poly-L-lactide-containing nanoparticles synergize adaptive and innate immunometabolism to alleviate heart fibrosis

metadata.summary: The prevalence of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) is increasing, with growing evidence implicating the intrauterine environment as a critical regulator of fetal brain development. Gestational perturbations such as maternal stress can increase NDD risk; however, the mechanism(s) by which prenatal maternal stress reshape fetal neurodevelopment remain unclear. Accordingly, the objective of my project was to characterize how maternal cold stress exposure during pregnancy disrupts neural stem and progenitor cell (NSPC) developmental programs in the fetus and the impact this has on neurodevelopment in the hypothalamus. Pregnant mice were exposed to 4°C for 30 minutes daily from embryonic day 11.5 (E11.5) to E15.5—a critical period of neurodevelopment in the hypothalamus. To assess how maternal cold stress impacts neural stem cell (NSC) behaviours, we employed the neurosphere assay, quantifying the number and size of primary and secondary neurospheres as a measure of NSC proliferation and self-renewal, respectively. Our findings revealed no change in NSC proliferation or self-renewal when comparing control and maternal cold stress male and female neurospheres. However, differentiation of dissociated NSCs revealed that neurons from both sexes had longer axons following maternal cold stress exposure. Interestingly, only male-derived cultures exhibited a significant increase in the number TUJ1+ neurons in response to maternal cold stress exposure, whereas only female-derived maternal cold stress cultures showed enhanced dendritic arborization. To explore the molecular basis of these changes, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing on E15.5 fetal hypothalamic NSPCs. Analysis of differentially expressed genes uncovered basal sex differences between the transcriptional signatures of control male and female Cycling NSPCs and suggested that maternal cold stress shifts female Cycling NSPCs toward a more male-like transcriptional profile. Gene ontology analysis revealed that maternal cold stress upregulates pathways linked to neuronal growth, development, and GABAergic neuron differentiation, but only in females. Importantly, ligand-receptor analysis suggested that maternal cold stress exposure disrupts neurodevelopmental programs through altered cell-cell signalling within Cycling NSPCs predominantly in females. These findings demonstrate that prenatal maternal cold stress exposure drives sex-specific effects on fetal neurodevelopment and uncover distinct cellular pathways that may contribute to sex differences seen in the presentation and risk of many NDDs.

observations.title: Prenatal maternal cold stress exposure drives sex-specific neurodevelopmental disruptions in the fetal hypothalamus

metadata.summary: Background: Hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) may extend donor heart preservation beyond conventional storage durations. We evaluated early graft function and myocardial cellular and metabolic integrity following porcine heart transplantation after 20 hours of HOPE.  Methods: Ten donor hearts underwent various preservation conditions: static cold storage (SCS) for 4 hours (n=2), HOPE for 4 hours (n=3), and HOPE for 20 hours (n=5), followed by heart transplantation (HT) in recipient pigs. Following implant and reperfusion, graft function was assessed over 3 hours by serial echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, optical flow analysis, and vasoactive support scoring; myocardial tissue was analyzed by histopathology, flow cytometry, mitochondrial respirometry, transcriptomics, and proteomics.  Results: Ejection fraction, right atrial pressure and systolic blood pressure did not differ significantly between groups, and no graft met criteria for primary graft dysfunction. LV contractility was within normal range with comparable vasoactive support among all groups. Preservation-associated weight gain was greatest after HOPE 20h, and histopathology showed comparable findings with edema present in all cohorts, without fibrosis, thrombosis, or necrosis. Cardiomyocyte viability was preserved across all groups (HOPE 20h, 86%, HOPE 4h, 81%, and SCS 4h, 77%). Maximal oxygen consumption rate was elevated in HOPE 20h versus HOPE 4h and SCS 4h (p<0.01), while basal and non-mitochondrial respiration were similar. Transcriptomics and proteomics revealed minimal differences in gene and pathway expression among groups.   Conclusions: HOPE preserves donor heart viability, mitochondrial integrity, and ventricular function after 20 hours of ischemia in a porcine model, without evidence of primary graft dysfunction, supporting extended preservation for heart transplantation. Edema, recovery of function, and metabolic responses warrant further investigation with longer-term monitoring.

observations.title: Twenty-Hour Hypothermic Oxygenated Perfusion Preserves Myocardial Viability and Bioenergetics with No Primary Graft Dysfunction After Porcine Heart Transplantation

metadata.summary: Developing arteries must withstand pulsatile blood flow while remaining sufficiently flexible to accommodate changing hemodynamic demands. Endothelial interactions with perivascular cells and extracellular matrix are essential for this balance, but the signaling mechanisms that coordinate them remain incompletely understood. We previously showed that SH2 domain protein E (She), an endothelial adaptor protein implicated in ABL signaling, limits the size of the dorsal aorta (DA) in zebrafish embryos. Here, we investigated why zebrafish she mutants subsequently develop DA collapse and circulatory failure at 4–5 days post-fertilization. Before circulatory failure, the mutant DA retained an approximately circular cross-section and showed no detectable changes in the endothelial cell geometry, but exhibited increased distensibility during the cardiac cycle. Mutants had fewer perivascular stromal cells between the DA and posterior cardinal vein, smaller perivascular col1a1 and col5a1 expression domains, and reduced col1a1 transcript level. Single-cell RNA sequencing independently identified a reduced relative abundance of perivascular fibroblast subpopulation. In contrast, DA-associated mural cell numbers, laminin immunoreactivity, and local col4a1 transcript levels were not detectably altered. Ablation of pdgfrb-positive cells largely prevented DA narrowing and circulatory failure, while the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside provided partial rescue. These findings support a contribution of mural cell-dependent vascular tone to collapse of the mechanically vulnerable DA. Mutants also exhibited cardiac chamber enlargement, increased atrial and bulbus arteriosus deformation, atrioventricular regurgitation, and increased Elastin B accumulation in the enlarged bulbus arteriosus. However, endocardial-specific She expression failed to rescue circulatory failure, supporting its requirement in vascular endothelium. Together, these findings link She function to perivascular fibroblast abundance, fibrillar collagen-gene expression, and arterial stability. They support a model in which impaired perivascular support renders the developing DA susceptible to mural cell-associated collapse, extending the role of She from early vessel-size regulation to maintenance of vascular function.

observations.title: SH2 Domain Protein E sustains perivascular fibroblasts to maintain arterial stability
